The low end of a range is CLOSED, meaning full left or full down. If an axis runs backwards, or its travel needs tuning for the mount you have built, calibrate it with holo endpoints rather than rewiring — the values are saved in NVS under the pin, so they follow the wiring. See The holoprojector.

items.title: Going limp
items.text: The servos are not driven at boot, and stay limp until something moves them. holo off, or servo_off all, stops driving them again; the next move picks up from wherever they were left. This matters mechanically — a servo held against a hard stop for hours will cook itself.

items.title: Install
items.text:
The firmware goes onto the board over its USB-C port. There are three ways to do it, and all three write the same four images: the bootloader, the partition table, the boot selection and the application.

  • In the browser: nothing to install. Needs desktop Chrome, Edge or Opera.
  • With esptool: works in any browser and on any OS, with no ESP-IDF, using the images from a release.
  • From source: build it yourself with ESP-IDF, for changing the firmware.

On a board that already runs Holo Player, each way can either update it or overwrite it completely:

Settings (NVS) Clips and images (/data) Update kept kept Fresh install / complete overwrite erased erased

An update keeps them because it writes nothing outside the four images. A fresh install erases the whole flash first. That is the right choice for a board that is blank or runs something else, and the fix for a board in a state you would rather not keep.

items.title: Install the firmware
items.text:
In the browserWith esptoolFrom source

The installer can't run on this page. Opened from the documentation zip? Browsers won't run it from a file: run python3 serve.py in the unzipped folder, as described below. Otherwise it needs JavaScript. Or use one of the other tabs.

  1. Connect the board's USB-C port to the computer, then press Connect to the board and pick its port. The bridge is a CH343P: on macOS it appears as cu.wchusbserial… (or cu.usbmodem…), on Windows as a COM port named USB-SERIAL CH343. If nothing is listed, see Troubleshooting.
  2. The installer reads the board and says what it found: the Holo Player version in each firmware slot and which one boots, other firmware, or a blank flash. Nothing is written yet.

  3. Choose what to do. The installer preselects the sensible choice.

    Update: keep settings and clips is the default when the board runs Holo Player. It is unavailable when this release divides the flash up differently from the firmware on the board, since kept data could then be misread. It warns when the release is older than what is installed.

    Fresh install is the default for a blank board or other firmware. It is called Complete overwrite when the board runs Holo Player, and then asks you to confirm, because it deletes every clip and setting.

  4. Press Install. Every image is checked against its SHA-256 before anything is written, and every region is read back and checked after. Erasing the whole flash takes about 30 seconds; writing takes about 30 more at the default speed.

  5. The installer restarts the board and shows its boot messages. When the board reports the version just installed, it's done, and the port is free for a terminal.

If writing fails part way, the board may not start until an install completes. Connect and install again. Setting a lower baud rate under Advanced helps with a poor cable or hub.

Installing without internet access

The documentation zip attached to each release contains the same installer and firmware. A browser won't use a serial port from a page opened as a file, so unzip it and run the small server inside:

python3 serve.py

It serves the folder on localhost only, fetches nothing from the internet, and opens this page, where the installer then works. Stop it with Ctrl-C. To host the documentation on an internal web server instead, serve it over HTTPS: browsers only allow serial ports on secure pages.

For Firefox, Safari, or anywhere else the browser installer can't run. You need Python and esptool:

pip install esptool

From the release you want, download the four images and SHA256SUMS. Replace vX.Y.Z in the commands below with its version. The documentation zip has the same files in its firmware/ folder. Then check that the download is intact:

sha256sum --ignore-missing -c SHA256SUMS           # Linux
shasum -a 256 --ignore-missing -c SHA256SUMS       # macOS

Update, keeping settings and clips:

esptool --chip esp32s3 -p PORT -b 460800 write-flash \
    0x0     holo-player-fw-vX.Y.Z-bootloader.bin \
    0x8000  holo-player-fw-vX.Y.Z-partition-table.bin \
    0xe000  holo-player-fw-vX.Y.Z-ota-data-initial.bin \
    0x10000 holo-player-fw-vX.Y.Z.bin

Fresh install or complete overwrite: erase first, then run the same command.

esptool --chip esp32s3 -p PORT erase-flash

PORT is /dev/cu.wchusbserial… on macOS, /dev/ttyUSB0 on Linux, COM3 on Windows. Only update a board whose partition layout is the release's. When a release changes it, its notes say so, and a fresh install is needed.

The firmware builds with ESP-IDF 6.1 for the esp32s3 target. There is no Arduino path.

1. Get the source. Three things the build needs live in git submodules — the shared console commands, the GIF decoder and libcanard, the Cyphal/CAN transport — so clone recursively:

git clone --recursive https://github.com/daveismith/holo-player-fw

In a clone that already exists, and again after pulling a change that adds one:

git submodule update --init --recursive

Without them the build fails: at main/CMakeLists.txt, which requires the console components by name, or at components/animatedgif, whose sources are another. The kit carries the Cyphal node's libcanard and Cyphal's public data types as submodules of its own (git submodule update --init --recursive); the data types aren't needed to build: only to regenerate the holo's Cyphal C headers (tools/gen_dsdl.py) and to run its hardware tests (tests/hardware/).

2. Build.

idf.py build

sdkconfig is not committed. Everything the build needs is in sdkconfig.defaults, so the first build writes a fresh sdkconfig from it — see Configuration for what is set and why. The component manager restores managed_components/ from dependencies.lock on the first build, which needs network access.

3. Flash. This is an update: settings and clips are kept.

idf.py -p /dev/cu.wchusbserial5B910448341 flash monitor

For a fresh install or complete overwrite, add erase-flash before flash.

Use your own port: /dev/cu.wchusbserial… on macOS, /dev/ttyUSB0 on Linux, COM3 on Windows.

The board's USB-C port goes through a CH343P USB-UART bridge to UART0 at 115200 baud. Its DTR/RTS lines drive the auto-download circuit, so none of these needs button presses. The ESP32-S3's native USB pins are not connected on this board, which is why every tool here talks to a serial port rather than USB.

Installing over USB always returns to the first slot

All three ways write the application to ota_0 and reset the boot selection. That is worth knowing if you have been updating over the console, which alternates between two slots — see Updating over serial.

items.title: Check it
items.text:
The console comes up on the same port the firmware was installed over, at 115200 baud. The browser installer lets go of the port once it is done; only one program can hold it at a time. At the prompt:

version

It reports the firmware's own version, when it was built, and the chip it is running on. A release reports its tag, such as v0.1.0; a build from an untagged working tree reports the commit it came from, with -dirty appended if there were uncommitted changes.

help

lists every command. The screen stays off until something is shown on it — try screen colour red, then screen clear.

items.title: Line the screen up
items.text:
Before the panel is fixed behind a dome's lens, put up the alignment pattern:

screen calibration

A crosshair with an arrow pointing up, for centring the panel in the lens opening and getting its rotation right. Every clip afterwards is drawn on those axes, so this is worth doing while the board is still loose — see Mounting the screen.

items.title: Updating later
items.text: Once the bootloader is on the board, new firmware can be installed over the console without USB access, which matters when the board is mounted inside a droid. See Updating over serial.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
Build-time settings live in two places: choices you are meant to change, in idf.py menuconfig, and the settings the firmware needs to work at all, in sdkconfig.defaults.

sdkconfig itself is not committed. Everything the build needs is in sdkconfig.defaults, so a fresh clone builds correctly and a stale sdkconfig can always be deleted and regenerated.

items.title: Board: Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-1.28
items.text:
Option Default Does BOARD_LCD_PCLK_MHZ 80 LCD SPI clock, 10–80 MHz BOARD_TOUCH_ENABLE on Compile in the touch driver and the touch command BOARD_TOUCH_AUTOSTART off The default of the touch reporting setting (settings touch, touch.reporting in /api/v1/settings, the Cyphal register r2.touch.reporting): on in a build with it. A saved setting wins

The clock default is not arbitrary. The GC9A01 has no tearing-effect line on this board, so nothing synchronises a frame write to the panel's own ~60 Hz refresh. A full 240×240 RGB565 frame is 921,600 bits: 23 ms at 40 MHz, which is longer than one refresh, so a new frame is seen sweeping down the screen — and 11.5 ms at 80 MHz, which fits inside one. Drop to 40 only if the picture shows corruption at 80.

items.title: LED strip (NeoPixel)
items.text:
Option Default Does LEDS_GPIO 16 Data line; 16 is P2 pin 8 LEDS_COUNT 16 LEDs on the strip LEDS_SPEED 800 kHz 800 kHz for WS2812/WS2812B/SK6812; 400 kHz for WS2811 LEDS_ORDER GRB Colour order on the wire; RGB if red and green come out swapped LEDS_BRIGHTNESS 100 Brightness at boot, 1–100

Two of these have consequences off the board

400 kHz on a WS2812 makes every frame full white, including the frame that turns the strip off. And at 100% brightness sixteen LEDs can draw about 1 A, which is more than the P2 header's VSYS pin should be asked for — keep it at 30 or below unless the strip has its own supply. Both are covered in Wiring the LED ring.

items.title: Holoprojector servos
items.text:
Option Default Does HOLO_SERVO1_GPIO 17 P2 pin 9 HOLO_SERVO2_GPIO 18 P2 pin 10 HOLO_SERVO1_MIN_US / _MAX_US 1150 / 1900 Servo 1's working travel HOLO_SERVO2_MIN_US / _MAX_US 1300 / 1950 Servo 2's working travel HOLO_PAN Servo 1 Which servo pans; the other tilts HOLO_SERVO_ABS_MIN_US / _MAX_US 1000 / 2000 Absolute limits no servo is driven outside

The minimum of a working range is CLOSED — full left for pan, full down for tilt. Each servo's travel must lie inside the absolute range. These defaults are the servos' real travel rather than a guess, which is why motion works before anything is calibrated; see The holoprojector.

items.title: holo-player-fw
items.text: Option Default Does CONSOLE_STORE_HISTORY on Keep command history in /data/history.txt across restarts CONSOLE_IGNORE_EMPTY_LINES on Ignore blank input rather than treating it as end-of-input

items.title: Wi-Fi fallback
items.text:
Option Default Does HOLO_WIFI_FALLBACK_AP on Turn the access point on when the board can't join a network at start. With wifi auto off, only when there is no network to rejoin HOLO_WIFI_FALLBACK_AP_MIN 5 Minutes it stays on, at start or from the button, before it turns itself off HOLO_WIFI_JOIN_WAIT_S 20 Seconds a join has before the access point comes on instead HOLO_WIFI_BUTTON_GPIO 0 The button (to ground) that rejoins, or turns the access point on, when the board is off the network; 0 is BOOT. -1 for none

See With no network.

items.title: Host link
items.text:
The compiled-in defaults, which the saved link settings override.

Option Default Does HOSTLINK_MODE Off Off, UART, or RS485 HOSTLINK_PROTOCOL Either JSON lines, native frames, or either, told apart by the first byte HOSTLINK_PIN_A / _B / _C 21 / 33 / 15 P2 pins 11, 12 and 7 HOSTLINK_BAUD 115200 UART and RS485 HOSTLINK_ADDRESS 1 The board's address on UART and RS485, 1–223 HOSTLINK_I2C_ADDRESS 0x42 The board's I2C address (for the I2C link, not in the firmware yet) HOSTLINK_TASK_STACK 10240 The link task's stack: a request runs on it

items.title: Console WiFi commands
items.text: The cmd_wifi component adds its own menu, for the NVS namespace saved networks are kept in and how hard the board tries to reconnect when a link drops.

items.title: sdkconfig.defaults
items.text:
What is set, and why it matters here:

Area Setting Why Target esp32s3 The only supported chip Optimisation COMPILER_OPTIMIZATION_PERF (-O2) Video decoding is the hot path, and the decoder benchmark is only fair at -O2 Flash 16 MB, QIO, 80 MHz The board's part PSRAM Quad, 80 MHz, SPIRAM_USE_MALLOC Holds a whole frame in the fallback decode path CPU 240 MHz Frame budget Partitions Custom, partitions.csv Two OTA slots and an 11 MB volume Rollback BOOTLOADER_APP_ROLLBACK_ENABLE Console-installed images boot on trial; see Updating over serial Console UART0 at 115200, secondary console off The CH343P bridge is the board's only USB path UART UART_ISR_IN_IRAM Keeps the RX FIFO drained during XMODEM transfers even while a flash operation has the cache off FreeRTOS Trace facility, stats formatting, run-time stats tasks and top Flash counters SPI_FLASH_ENABLE_COUNTERS flash-stats Core dumps To the coredump partition, checked at boot Post-mortem after a crash Touch ESP_LCD_TOUCH_CST816S_DISABLE_READ_ID A CST816S only answers on I2C while touched, so reading its ID at init always fails IPv6 LWIP_IPV6_AUTOCONFIG SLAAC addresses as well as link-local LittleFS 4096-byte cache, 256-byte read/write, PSRAM-prefer, LITTLEFS_MMAP_PARTITION Tuned for sequential reads of large clips

The LittleFS settings are the ones worth understanding. The component's defaults — 128-byte reads and 512-byte caches — measure about 2 MB/s. Memory-mapping the partition serves reads through the flash cache rather than esp_flash_read(), which would stall both cores for the duration of every read, exactly as a write does. See Video internals.

items.title: Partition table
items.text:
partitions.csv, derived from the Flash_PNG layout less phy_init (the PHY init data is built into the application). nvs takes its 4 KB so that otadata keeps its original offset.

Name Type Offset Size Holds nvs data 36K 20K Saved Wi-Fi networks, servo calibration otadata data 56K 8K Which application slot boots ota_0 app 64K 2304K Application slot 0 ota_1 app — 2304K Application slot 1 coredump data — 64K Core dumps storage data 5M 11M LittleFS, mounted at /data

Two application slots of 2.25 MB each are what make updating over the console possible: the image being received always goes into the slot that is not running.

items.title: Console commands
items.text:
The console is the board's whole interface. It runs on UART0 at 115200 baud, reached over the USB-C port. Type help for the full list with hints; this page is the annotated version.

In desktop Chrome, Edge or Opera, the ▶ beside a command tries it on a board connected to the computer. The board in the browser has every command the board lists, and its console.

Command history is kept in /data/history.txt and survives a restart.

A colour is written the same way everywhere

screen colour and leds colour both take a name (red, orange, …), #RRGGBB or bare RRGGBB, or three decimal values as R,G,B or R G B. screen colour additionally accepts a raw RGB565 value written as 0x….

items.title: The board
items.text:
Command Does screen [colour <c> \| calibration \| clear] Show a solid colour or the alignment crosshair, or clear the screen. Alone, reports what is showing, including a clip or an image. The screen is off — panel asleep, backlight off — whenever nothing is lcd [bl <0-100> \| bench [frames]] LCD hardware: power state, backlight level while on, and a fill-rate benchmark touch [on\|off\|status] CST816S touch reporting, for now: on or off until the next start, not saved (settings touch is what the board starts with: off unless set). Prints down/move/up with x,y imu [-r <hz>] [-n <count>] \| imu id Streams accelerometer (g), gyro (dps) and temperature until a key is pressed. imu id reports the part and the address it answered on

screen calibration (or screen calib) draws a centred crosshair with an arrow pointing up, for lining the panel up behind a dome's lens — see Mounting the screen.

touch is only present when BOARD_TOUCH_ENABLE is set, which it is by default. See Configuration.

items.title: Images
items.text:
Command Does image show <file> Show a PNG, baseline JPEG or GIF, centred. It stays until something else takes the screen. An animated GIF plays, looping as the file says, and leaves its last frame up if it stops image info <file> What the file is — format, size, bit depth; for a GIF, frames, loops and length — without decoding it or touching the panel

An image larger than 240×240 is refused rather than scaled. Transparency is composited over black. An animated GIF plays on the video player's task, so video stop and video status work on it. Full detail in Images.

items.title: Video
items.text:
Command Does video play <file> [loop] [frame] Play a Motion-JPEG QuickTime clip, centred, on the clip's own timing. loop repeats it; frame forces whole-frame decoding video stop Stop a clip or an animated GIF, and turn the screen off video status Per-frame read, decode, decode-plus-draw and paint times, for a clip or an animated GIF video info <file> What the file contains, without playing it video verify <file> [step] Decode sample frames both ways and compare them byte for byte

Full detail in Video clips.

items.title: LEDs
items.text:
Command Does leds What the strip is showing, plus the hardware it is driving leds colour <c> A solid colour leds off Off leds wipe [<c>] [loop] Each LED to the colour in turn, 250 ms apart. White if no colour given leds rainbow [loop] The colour wheel five times round the ring in 12.8 s leds flicker [<c>] The colour flickering like a failing hologram, until something else. White if no colour given leds pulse [<c>] [-p <ms>] The colour fading up and down once a period (200–60000 ms; 2000), until something else. White if no colour given leds blink [<c>] [-p <ms>] The colour on for half a period and off for the other half (1000 ms unless given), until something else … -l <pct>, … -t <s> The level, a share of the brightness (0–100), after any mode but off (a wipe's or a rainbow's after its loop); and a time (0.1–3600 s) after which the ring goes back to what it was doing, after colour, off, flicker, pulse or blink leds bright <1-100> Brightness, applied live

Full detail in LED patterns.

items.title: The holoprojector
items.text:
Command Does holo Status: the light, the current motion, and both axes holo <verb> … center, move, nudge, twitch, wag, nod, scan, circle, stop, off, endpoints. holo help lists the options servo_list [-o wide] Both servos, with their absolute and working ranges servo_move <ident> <pos> [-p] Move one servo, by percentage or raw pulse servo_sweep <ident>… [-t n] Sweep one or more servos servo_config <ident> <min> <max> [-i] Set a servo's working range, with optional invert servo_off <ident>\|all Stop driving a servo, so it goes limp servo_register Re-attach both servos; harmless to repeat

holo led and holo leia's light half do nothing on this board — there is no light attached. Full detail in The holoprojector.

items.title: Scenes and settings
items.text:
Command Does scene [list] The saved scenes, and which the board starts with scene show <name> One scene, as JSON scene apply <name> Apply it: the screen, then the LEDs, then the holo scene end End the scene running to its end now, doing what it does then (go back, or all off) scene delete <name> Delete it; if the board started with it, it now starts with nothing scene boot [<name>\|--clear] The scene the board starts with; alone, which it is scene slot <name> [<1-255>\|--clear] The number a host on the host link applies it by; alone, which it is settings What the board starts with: the backlight, the LEDs' brightness and count, touch reporting, and the scene settings backlight <1-100> The backlight at start, and now settings brightness <1-100> The LEDs' brightness at start, and now settings leds <count> LEDs on the strip, from the next start settings touch on\|off Touch reporting at start, and now (the Cyphal register r2.touch.reporting is the same setting) settings reset Back to the firmware's defaults, applied now; scenes are kept

A scene is what the screen shows, what the LEDs do and how the holo moves, saved together by name; a scene may have any of the three. Scenes are made with the HTTP API or the web app — a scene's JSON is too long to type here — and the console applies and chooses them. A name may contain spaces: scene apply amber glow.

items.title: Files and firmware
items.text:
Command Does fs ls\|df\|stat\|mkdir\|rmdir\|rm\|mv\|cat\|hexdump\|sha256\|bench … The LittleFS volume at /data. Paths are relative to it fs put [-f] [-b baud] <path> [size] Receive a file over XMODEM-1K fs get [-b baud] [-s 128\|1024] <path> Send a file over XMODEM-1K ota [status] Both application slots: what is in each, its version, and which runs and boots ota put [-b baud] [-n] [-d] <size> Receive a new image into the slot that is not running ota pull [-n] [-s] [-f] [--sha256 <hex>] <url\|channel> Download a new image over Wi-Fi: a release channel such as latest, a release's manifest, or an image's URL ota activate [-n] [slot] Make the staged image, or the image in a slot, the boot image, and restart into it

The host side of fs put, fs get and ota put is tools/fs_xfer.py in esp-console-kit — see Files on the board and Updating the firmware.

items.title: System
items.text:
Command Does version The running firmware's version and build, and the chip it is on restart Software reset free Free heap heap Heap details membench Memory throughput benchmark flash-stats [reset] Flash operation counters tasks Every FreeRTOS task top Task CPU usage over an interval log_level Change a log tag's level at runtime gpio get <n> \| set <n> 0\|1 \| release <n> Read or drive a pin. Pins the board owns are refused, with the reason deep_sleep Enter deep sleep light_sleep Enter light sleep

tasks and top need the FreeRTOS trace and run-time-stats options, and flash-stats needs the flash counters; all are enabled in sdkconfig.defaults.

items.title: The host link
items.text:
See the host link.

Command Does link The transport, its pins and settings, the counters, and the events asked for. On CAN, the pins and who has them link mode <off\|uart\|rs485\|can> [-b <baud>] [-a <address>] The transport, from the next restart; -b the baud rate, -a the address, 1–223. can gives the pins to the Cyphal node link proto <auto\|json\|native> What UART and RS485 accept link address <1-223> The board's address on UART and RS485 link groups [<group>…\|--clear] The groups it acts for, 1–31, up to 8 link pins <a> <b> <c> The GPIOs for roles A, B and C, from the next restart link events [<kind>…\|--none] [--push\|--keep] The events it reports from the start: clip_ended, scene_ended, touch, or a resource's changes (screen, leds, scene, …) link log [on\|off] Print everything the link sends and receives link reset Back to the firmware's defaults

items.title: CAN and Cyphal
items.text:
See the board on Cyphal, and the wiring.

Command Does link mode can The host link's pins go to the Cyphal node, from the next restart cyphal The node's state, its node-ID, name, unique ID and plug-and-play pseudo-ID, the bus's state, and the counters cyphal id <0-127>\|auto A fixed node-ID, or one from the bus by plug-and-play. From the node's next start cyphal name <name>\|--reset The name uavcan.node.GetInfo reports: r2.dome.holo.front until changed. From the node's next start cyphal bitrate <125k\|250k\|500k\|1m> The bus's bitrate. From the node's next start cyphal restart Stop the node and start it again, with the settings as they now are: also how a node that stopped over a node-ID in use is started again cyphal reset Back to the firmware's defaults: plug-and-play, the default name, 1 Mbit/s, and every port's default ID cyphal register The node's Cyphal registers: each one's value, type and flags, and the value in use when a write waits for the node's next start cyphal register <name> One register cyphal register <name> <value>… Write one, as uavcan.register.Access does, with the same checks, saved: a number for a port or the node-ID (65535 for off or plug-and-play), one or two for the bitrate, a word for the name, from the node's next start; the holo's own (r2.holo.* endpoints, release and settle time, r2.touch.reporting: numbers, or 0 and 1 for bits) at once can Raw CAN frames, for testing the wiring while the node is off: whether it's running, the bus's state and error counters, and frames sent and received. While the node runs it only reports, and its sub-commands refuse can start [-b <bitrate>] [--listen\|--selftest] Start the controller. --listen receives without sending or acknowledging; --selftest receives its own frames and needs no second node can stop Stop, and release the pins; dump and echo go off can send <id>#<hex> Send one frame: an 11-bit ID as up to three hex digits, a 29-bit one as eight, and up to 8 data bytes can dump [on\|off] Print every frame received (on if neither is given) can echo [on\|off] Send every frame received straight back, with 1 added to its ID: the other end of tools/can_check.py echo can recover Bring the controller back from bus-off

items.title: Networking
items.text:
Wi-Fi is what the web app and updates over Wi-Fi use; nothing else needs it.

Command Does wifi [on\|off] Turn the radio on or off wifi auto [on\|off] Whether the board rejoins its last network when it starts; on until turned off. Alone, says which wifi scan The networks in range, strongest first, and which are saved wifi ap [on\|off] [--ssid <ssid>] [--pass <passphrase>] The board's own access point, holo-xxxx at 192.168.4.1: on or off (off again at every boot, unless the board can't join a network: then on for 5 minutes, as after a press of BOOT), and its name and passphrase. Alone, shows them, and how long it has left web [on\|off] The web app and its API: where to reach it. off stops the server, and stays off across restarts web password <password>\|--clear Changes over the web need this password, as do downloading files and reading the web settings web hostname <name>\|--clear The board's name on the network: <name>.local web cors [add <origin>\|remove <origin>\|reset\|none] Which other sites' pages may call the API from a browser (CORS). Alone, lists them wifi_save <ssid> [pass] Remember a network. The board rejoins the last one at boot wifi_forget Forget a saved network wifi_known List saved networks join Join a network without saving it wifi_link Link status wifi_ps Power-save mode wifi_txpower Transmit power ip addr Addresses, with -f inet\|inet6\|link and -s ping Ping a host iperf Throughput test traceroute Trace a route dig DNS lookup

items.title: NVS and I2C
items.text:
Command Does nvs_set / nvs_get Read and write a key nvs_erase / nvs_erase_namespace Erase a key, or a whole namespace nvs_namespace Select the namespace the other commands act on nvs_list List what is stored nvs_inventory [-x] Every stored setting and whether a backup holds it, or why not; -x lists the rules nvs_export [path] The settings as a backup file: printed, or written to /data/backup/<name> (a path starting / is on the volume, as fs takes it) nvs_import [-n] [--replace] [--ignore-excluded] [--other-board] [--no-snapshot] [-r] <path\|url\|-> Restore a backup: a name in /data/backup, a path starting / on the volume, a URL, or the console (-). The whole file is checked before anything is written; -n only shows what would change. Restart afterwards (-r) i2cconfig Configure the bus the I2C tools use i2cdetect Scan the bus i2cget / i2cset Read and write a register i2cdump Dump a device's registers

The I2C tools borrow the bus the firmware already created on port 0, and never tear down a bus they did not create. Remember that the touch controller only answers while the screen is being touched.

Servo calibration lives in the servo NVS namespace, keyed by pin. Saved Wi-Fi networks live in their own namespace, set in menuconfig. Backing up the settings covers nvs_inventory, nvs_export and nvs_import.

items.title: Where these come from
items.text:
The board-specific commands — screen, lcd, touch, imu, video, image, leds — are in this repository, under components/. Everything else comes from the esp-console-kit submodule, whose README is the reference for the commands this page only summarises.

tools/check_command_docs.py checks that every command the firmware registers appears on this site, so the tables above cannot quietly fall behind the code.

items.title: Cyphal interface
items.text:
This is the specification of what the board does on a Cyphal/CAN bus: every port, every type and its fields, every register and every command. How to use it is on the board on Cyphal.

Node management uses Cyphal's standard types, from public_regulated_data_types. The holo's own types are r2.holo.*, in a repository of their own, r2_cyphal_dsdl, which a controller (the dome panel, an app on Linux) generates its code from too. They are at version 0.1, unstable: they become 1.0 when the dome panel is first written against them, and from then on a type that has shipped is never changed, only given a new version.

items.title: The node's ports
items.text:
Function Type Port Sent or served Heartbeat uavcan.node.Heartbeat.1.0 subject 7509 Once a second. Its health is advisory while the holo can't move (below) Node information uavcan.node.GetInfo.1.0 service 430 Its name, version and unique ID Plug-and-play uavcan.pnp.NodeIDAllocationData.1.0 subject 8166 Only while it asks for a node-ID The ports it uses uavcan.node.port.List.1.0 subject 7510 Every 10 seconds, the first as the node goes online. Below Registers uavcan.register.Access.1.0, uavcan.register.List.1.0 services 384, 385 Below Restart, factory reset, identify uavcan.node.ExecuteCommand.1.3 service 435 Below The clips and images uavcan.file.List.0.2, uavcan.file.GetInfo.0.2 services 406, 405 The files on the storage volume: names, sizes, times. Read only. Below What the holo is doing r2.holo.Status.0.1 subject 2300 Within 250 ms of a change, and once a second What happened r2.holo.Event.0.1 subject 2301 As it happens Where the axes are r2.holo.Axes.0.1 subject 2302 Ten times a second while the holo moves, once a second at rest Where the axes go r2.holo.Axes.0.1 subject 2303, subscribed A stream of setpoints Motions r2.holo.Motion.0.1 service 100 The light r2.holo.Light.0.1 service 101 Scenes r2.holo.Scene.0.1 service 102 The screen r2.holo.Screen.0.1 service 103 The LED ring r2.holo.Ring.0.1 service 104 The scene list r2.holo.ListScenes.0.1 service 105 A file's details r2.holo.MediaInfo.0.1 service 106 Optional in the types (a board may leave it out); this one serves it

The standard ports' IDs are fixed by the standard. The r2.holo ports' are defaults, in Cyphal's unregulated ranges, which registers change. r2_cyphal_dsdl's ports/holo.csv holds the same defaults for a program to read.

Port name Kind Default ID Priority status Published subject 2300 low event Published subject 2301 nominal axes Published subject 2302 high setpoint Subscribed subject 2303 fast motion Served service 100 nominal light Served service 101 nominal scene Served service 102 nominal screen Served service 103 nominal ring Served service 104 nominal list_scenes Served service 105 nominal media_info Served service 106 nominal

The priority is the one the board sends at; a client calls a service at the same. Services are addressed to the board's node-ID, so two holos on one bus serve them on the same IDs without trouble. A subject is shared by the whole bus: two holos can publish status on 2300 (a receiver tells them apart by node-ID), but two holos subscribed to setpoint on 2303 move together, so each gets a subject of its own.

items.title: The port list
items.text:
uavcan.node.port.List names the ports the node really has while it runs, at the optional priority, as the type asks. A port's number changes only when the node starts (the registers apply from then), so the list does too: it goes out as the node goes online, and every 10 seconds after. With the registers at their defaults it holds:

Publishers 7509 (the heartbeat), 7510 (the port list), 2300 (status), 2301 (event), 2302 (axes) Subscribers 2303 (setpoint) Clients None Servers 100 (motion), 101 (light), 102 (scene), 103 (screen), 104 (ring), 105 (list_scenes), 106 (media_info), 384 and 385 (registers), 405 and 406 (the file services), 430 (GetInfo), 435 (ExecuteCommand)

Each r2.holo port is in it on the number its register held as the node started; a port turned off (65535) is never in it. The servers are a bit mask of every service-ID, so the list is 160 bytes, 24 frames, whatever it holds.

items.title: Health
items.text: The heartbeat's health is advisory while the holo can't move, for the reasons Status gives in ready and why, and nominal otherwise. The node's mode is always operational. On this board the holo can't move only when one of its servos didn't attach at the start (not fitted), or the holo engine didn't start (Status then reads not fitted for no axis in particular): an axis without saved endpoints moves over its default travel, so it doesn't make the health advisory (Status's calibrated still says whether its endpoints are saved). A board with no holo wired to it at all can't tell: its servos are outputs that read nothing back, so it reports the holo ready, and nominal.

items.title: Conventions
items.text:
• Units are in the names: _ms is milliseconds, _us microseconds. A percent is 0–100 unless the field says otherwise.
  • Zero means the default. A request field left at 0 takes its default wherever it has one, so a request that is all zeros asks for every default. Where 0 is a value in its own right (a move's duration, the light's level, the backlight, the ring's off), the field is optional instead: an array of at most one ([<=1]), empty for the default.
  • Times in Status are spans from the moment it was sent, *_age_ms back and *_remaining_ms forward, never stamps, so the receiver's clock needn't be the board's. NEVER (0xFFFFFFFF) is "no such time".
  • Paths are from the root of the storage volume (/clips/intro.mov), as uavcan.file.Path.2.0: up to 255 bytes in the type, at most 159 on this board.
  • Names of scenes are 1–32 of A-Z a-z 0-9, space, _, . and -.
  • Sizes. Classic CAN carries 7 bytes of a transfer a frame. A transfer of up to 7 bytes is one frame; a longer one adds a 2-byte CRC. Sizes and bus load has each type's.

items.title: Status
items.text:
r2.holo.Status.0.1, published on status: everything the holo is doing, in one message, so that each is a consistent snapshot. It goes out within 250 ms of a change, never more than four times a second, and once a second whatever changes. A change is a change to any field but a time or a clip's progress (*_age_ms, *_remaining_ms, shown, passes), which the once-a-second message keeps current. The board builds it from the same state GET /api/v1/holo, GET /api/v1/leds, GET /api/v1/screen and GET /api/v1/scenes (its active) report. Once another Status may go (250 ms after the last), it looks at the holo, the screen and the scene for a change every 50 ms; the ring tells it of its own changes, as it tells the HTTP API's event stream. While the screen is being changed (a still decoding, a clip starting, the panel going to sleep), the board doesn't wait for it: screen stays as it was in the Status that goes meanwhile, and the change follows within 50 ms of its end. With nothing showing and no scene it is 86 bytes, 13 frames; with a 20-byte path and a 10-byte scene name, 116 bytes, 17 frames.

Field Type What it is holo state.Holo The holo's motion, below ring state.Ring The LED ring, which is also the holo's light, below screen state.Screen The screen, below scene state.Scene The scene running to its end, below event_seq uint16 The latest Event's seq; 0 before the first. A receiver that sees it move past the last event it got has missed one reporting_touch bool Touch events are on (the register r2.touch.reporting, or touch on)

items.title: The holo
items.text:
r2.holo.state.Holo.0.1: what GET /api/v1/holo and the console's holo report, and what the dome panel shows for a holo of its own.

Field Type What it is ready bool The holo could move now why Reason Why it can't, and the axis at fault. NONE when ready motion uint8 What runs now: 0 hold, 1 move (a center, move or nudge on its way), 2 twitch, 3 wag, 4 nod, 5 scan, 6 circle. The numbers of the host link's status block motion_age_ms uint32 Since the running motion began; NEVER while holding motion_remaining_ms uint32 Until a timed twitch or scan ends; NEVER with no limit, or while holding. A timed scan doesn't end by its time limit today (Motion's time_limit_ms): this counts down to 0 and stays there while the scan goes on stopped Reason Why the last motion ended early: an axis refused it partway, with the axis. NONE when it ended by itself, by stop, or by another motion stopped_motion uint8 Which motion that was, numbered as motion; 0 when stopped is NONE stopped_age_ms uint32 How long ago it stopped; NEVER when stopped is NONE horizontal, vertical state.Axis Each axis: fitted (its servo is there), calibrated (its endpoints are saved), inverted (closed is above open), placed (something has moved it since the board started, so Axes knows where it is). The engine places both axes together, so placed is the same for both last MotionSpec The last motion asked for, by anybody (Cyphal, the console, the host link, the HTTP API, a scene), as it was asked. A stop before any

The axes' positions are in Axes, not here.

items.title: The ring
items.text:
r2.holo.state.Ring.0.1: what GET /api/v1/leds reports (its timed and leia too), with the holo light's timed modes.

Field Type What it is now state.RingSetting What it is doing now remaining_ms uint32 A timed mode (a Light with a time limit, or a leia): until it goes back to after. NEVER when not timed after state.RingSetting What a timed mode goes back to. Meaningful only while remaining_ms isn't NEVER leia bool The timed flicker is a leia's, whoever asked for it

r2.holo.state.RingSetting.0.1:

Field Type What it is mode uint8 0 off, 1 solid, 2 wipe, 3 rainbow, 4 flicker, 5 pulse, 6 blink. The first five are the host link's LEDS numbers colour Colour r, g, b, 0–255. For every mode but off and rainbow brightness uint8 Percent, 0–100: how bright the ring is in this setting, its brightness (leds bright, GET /api/v1/leds's brightness) times the setting's level (its level), rounded period_ms uint16 Pulse, blink: 200–60000. 0 for the other modes loop bool Wipe, rainbow: again and again, rather than once

items.title: The screen
items.text:
r2.holo.state.Screen.0.1: what GET /api/v1/screen reports.

Field Type What it is showing uint8 0 nothing, 1 colour, 2 the calibration crosshair, 3 image, 4 clip (or animated GIF). The host link's status block numbers backlight uint8 Percent, 0–100 colour Colour When showing a colour: which. Black otherwise frames uint16 A clip: frames in one pass, from its header shown uint32 A clip: frames shown since it started, every pass passes uint16 A clip: times through so far (the JSON API's loops) plays uint16 A clip: times through in all, 1–1000; 0 for forever fps float16 A clip: frames a second, from its header path uavcan.file.Path.2.0 An image or a clip: the file. Empty otherwise

The clip's fields are 0 unless a clip shows.

items.title: The scene
items.text:
r2.holo.state.Scene.0.1: the scene running to its end, the JSON API's active (GET /api/v1/scenes). Only a scene whose then is restore or off runs to an end; a stay scene is applied and done, and leaves nothing running.

Field Type What it is running bool A scene is running to its end. Without one the fields below are 0 or empty then uint8 What follows its end: 1 restore, 2 off until_clip_ends bool It ends when its clip has played remaining_ms uint32 Until its duration_s is up; NEVER when it has none slot uint8 Its slot, 1–255; 0 when it has none name uint8[<=32] Its name

items.title: Event
items.text:
r2.holo.Event.0.1, published on event: one of the board's happenings, the same ones its JSON events and the host link's event records carry. Each is published once, as it happens, and there is no catching up: a receiver that misses one sees the gap in seq (or in Status's event_seq) and reads Status for what is going on now.

The board publishes them from its own record of happenings, the one the HTTP API's GET /api/v1/events?after= reads, which keeps the last 32: each is sent in turn, oldest first, with the number the record gave it, whatever started it (Cyphal, the console, the HTTP API, the host link or a scene). Happenings that come together (a scene applied over another can make four at once) wait in a queue of 8 for the bus, never replacing one another; if that queue is full, the one it refused is offered again a moment later, then at longer intervals while it stays full, and the rest are read from the record once it has gone. So none is lost while the record still has it, and one it no longer has shows as a jump in seq, as a missed one does. What happened before the node went online isn't sent: the first seq after it may be any number. Status's event_seq is the latest Event's, once it has gone into that queue.

Field Type What it is seq uint16 The board's number for this happening: 1–65535, then 1 again. One count for every happening on the board, shared with the web app and the host link what union One of the five below what Fields The JSON event clip_started plays uint16 (times through in all, 1–1000; 0 forever), frames uint16 (in one pass), fps float16, path clip_started clip_ended finished bool (played to its end; false when something replaced or stopped it, or it failed after it was accepted: it could not be read, or there was no memory for it), path clip_ended scene_started then uint8 (0 stay, 1 restore, 2 off), until_clip_ends bool, duration_ms uint32 (0 for none), slot uint8 (0 for none), name scene_started scene_ended then uint8, by uint8 (0 its clip played, 1 its time was up, 2 it was ended, 3 replaced: another scene or clip took over, or its clip failed after it was accepted, and its then wasn't done), slot uint8, name scene_ended screen_touch action uint8 (0 down, 1 up), x, y uint8 (0–239, from the top left). Only while touch reporting is on touch

The paths and names are carried whole, as the JSON events carry them, so a receiver needn't ask which clip ended. The order is the JSON events' order: a scene's clip starts just before its scene_started, and its scene_ended comes before what its then does.

items.title: Axes
items.text:
r2.holo.Axes.0.1: both axes, in hundredths of a percent of the calibrated travel each side of the centre. One frame.

Field Type What it is x int16 Horizontal: -10000 (closed, full left) to 10000 (open, full right); 0 the middle y int16 Vertical: -10000 (full down) to 10000 (full up)

NONE, -32768, is "no value" in either.

  • Published on axes: where the board last put each axis. A servo reports nothing back, so this is the position commanded, not one measured. NONE for an axis nothing has moved since the board started.
  • Subscribed on setpoint: a direct move. Each setpoint goes to the axes at once, with no easing, and stops the motion running first; the latest wins. NONE leaves that axis where it is. A value beyond ±10000 is held to it. While the holo can't move, a setpoint moves nothing and nothing answers it: Status says why.

The board does what the dome panel does for a ROS joint command: the motion running, if any, is stopped (Status then shows stop as the last motion asked for), and each axis given goes straight to its place through the servo layer, the call the holo engine's own moves end in. A setpoint received while the board is still carrying out the one before replaces it. The first setpoint after the board starts, before anything has placed the axes, goes through the engine as a move with no duration instead, so that the engine knows from then on where they are: an axis given as NONE in that one goes to the centre, where the engine takes an axis nothing has placed to be. A move is in whole percent, so once the engine has made it (within 20 ms) the same setpoint goes again the direct way, to its exact place; Status shows that move as the last motion asked for.

The resolution is finer than the holo's own, so nothing is lost either way: the engine places an axis in steps of 0.2 % of the travel each side (20 hundredths of a percent), and the pulse goes out in whole microseconds, which over this board's default travel is coarser still (0.27 % on pan, 0.31 % on tilt). A position published is the pulse sent, read back against the endpoints, so it can be up to half a percent short of the setpoint that put the axis there.

items.title: Services
items.text:
Every service answers with an Error as result: code 0 when it was done. A service does what the same request over the HTTP API or the host link does, through the same code, with the same refusals. A request that opens a file or waits (showing a file, applying a scene) is answered when it is done, a few hundred milliseconds at most; while the board is still working through the requests already sent to it, another is answered busy.

Scene, Screen and MediaInfo requests, the file services (and identify) are carried out one at a time, in the order they came, by a task of their own, so that a still being decoded, a file's header being read or the storage volume being busy with an upload never holds up the setpoints, Status or the other services. Two at most wait there; a third is answered busy (or, for uavcan.file.List, which can't say so, not at all). Motion, Light, Ring and ListScenes requests go on meanwhile, so one sent while a Scene or Screen request is still being carried out may be done before it: a controller that needs them in order waits for each response.

items.title: Motion
items.text:
r2.holo.Motion.0.1, on motion: start a motion of the holo, replacing the one running, as POST /api/v1/holo/motion and the console's holo do. The request is one field, motion, an r2.holo.MotionSpec.0.1; three frames.

Field Type What it is kind uint4 0 center, 1 move, 2 nudge, 3 twitch, 4 wag, 5 nod, 6 scan, 7 circle, 8 stop, 9 off. off stops, lets both axes go limp, and turns the light off: the release. On this board the light is the LED ring, which off turns off (the HTTP API's and the host link's off leave the ring alone) range uint7 Percent of the travel each side of the centre, 1–100. 0: the motion's default, twitch 60, scan 70, wag 50, nod 40, circle 50 count uint5 Wag, nod: cycles; circle: turns. 1–20. 0: wag 3, nod 2, circle 1 x int16 Move: −100 to 100, percent of the way from the centre to an endpoint, + right. Nudge: −200 to 200, relative. Needed by move and nudge y int16 As x; + is up period_ms uint16 A cycle of wag, nod, a turn of circle, a sweep of scan there and back: 200–60000. 0: wag 700, nod 800, circle 2400, scan 6000 interval_min_ms, interval_max_ms uint20 Twitch: the pause between glances, chosen between the two: each 100–600000, min no more than max. Both 0: 1000 to 5000. Both or neither time_limit_ms uint22 Twitch, scan: stop, and hold, after this long: 100–3600000. 0: no limit. A timed scan doesn't stop yet, over Cyphal, the console or the HTTP API alike: a fault in the shared holo engine, which looks at the time only between a motion's segments, and a scan has no gap between them duration_ms uint16[<=1] Center, move, nudge: how long to take, 0–10000; 0 is at once. Empty: by the distance, 250 ms and 500 ms more for each half of the travel

A field the motion doesn't use is ignored, whatever it holds. The odd widths are the ranges', to keep the request to three frames.

The board checks and starts the motion with the code POST /api/v1/holo/motion runs once it has read its JSON, as the host link's requests do: the fields the motion uses, the times in seconds as the route's interval_s and time_s are, and nothing else. So a motion is checked and refused as one over HTTP is, in the same words, which name the JSON API's fields:

result.code When bad request A field out of range: `range` is 1..100, `x` and `y` for move are -100..100, `interval_s` is [min, max], each 0.1..600, min first (one of the twitch's interval fields alone, or min over max), `time_s` is 0.1..3600. A kind that is none: `motion` is center, move, nudge, twitch, wag, nod, scan, circle, (the JSON API's words, cut, as every message is, to 64 bytes) not ready The holo can't move: result.reason says why (not fitted, uncalibrated) and which axis, and result.message says it in words: holo: refused, uncalibrated (tilt) busy The board is still working through four earlier requests: send it again

Nothing moves when a motion is refused. stop and off are never refused for the holo's state. This board moves an axis without saved endpoints over its default travel (the holo), so it never refuses one as uncalibrated: only an axis whose servo didn't attach is refused, as not fitted.

items.title: Light
items.text:
r2.holo.Light.0.1, on light: the holo's light, with the modes a dome panel's own holos have. On this board the light is the LED ring: on is the ring's solid, the others are the ring's modes of the same names, and Status's ring shows the result.

Field Type What it is mode uint8 0 off, 1 on, 2 pulse, 3 flicker, 4 blink, 5 leia period_ms uint16 Pulse, blink: 200–60000. 0: pulse 2000, blink 1000 time_limit_ms uint22 100–3600000: a timed mode, after which the ring goes back to what it was doing (mode, colour and level; Light never changes the ring's brightness). 0: for good; for leia, 30 s level uint8[<=1] Percent, 0–100: the share of the ring's brightness this mode lights at (0 lights nothing). Empty: 100. Ignored for off and leia colour Colour[<=1] The ring's colour for this mode. Empty: the colour it has now (white if it has never had one)

The level is a share of the ring's brightness (leds bright, the board's settings), not a brightness of its own: so the light at full is the ring at the brightness the user set, which keeps a ring powered from the board within its limit (the LED page) whatever a controller asks for. Status's ring shows the product, the brightness the ring lights at.

The board runs the code PATCH /api/v1/leds runs, with the same checks and words: a mode with its colour if given, the level (100 if not given), a pulse's or a blink's period, and time_s for a time limit (the LED page has the same from the console).

result.code When bad request `level` is 0..100, `period_ms` is 200..60000, `time_s` is 0.1..3600 (a time limit under 100 ms or over an hour), or a mode that is none: `mode` is off, on, pulse, flicker, blink or leia busy The board is still working through four earlier requests

Leia is the message from Leia: the light flickers at full for the time limit and then goes back to what it was doing, and the holo turns to the centre if it can. The light half always runs. The response's centred (bool) says whether the centre did too; when it didn't, result.code is still 0 and result.reason and result.message give the centre's refusal. The flicker is at level 100 in the colour given, or the ring's own; the centre is the motion route's center, at its default pace, so Status shows center as the last motion asked for. A time limit out of range refuses the whole request, before either half runs.

Another light or ring command during a timed mode replaces it, and the wait ends.

items.title: Scene
items.text:
r2.holo.Scene.0.1, on scene: apply a saved scene, or end the one running to its end, as POST /api/v1/scenes/apply and /scenes/end and the host link's SCENE and END do.

Field Type What it is action uint8 0 apply, 1 end slot uint8 Apply: the scene's slot, 1–255; 0 to apply it by name name uint8[<=32] Apply with slot 0: the scene's name

The board loads the scene saved with that slot or name and applies it with the code POST /api/v1/scenes/apply runs; end is POST /api/v1/scenes/end's. The refusals carry the HTTP API's words:

result.code When bad request action is none (`action` is 0 (apply) or 1 (end)); apply with slot 0 and no name (give `slot` (1..255), or `name` with slot 0); a name that can't be a scene's (give `name`: 1-32 letters, digits, spaces, _ . and -) not found No scene with that slot (no scene with slot 7) or name (no scene 'cantina'); for end, no scene running to its end (no scene is running to its end) not playable Its screen part can't be shown, its file missing included (screen: no such file: /clips/a.mov) not ready Its holo motion can't run

A part that fails stops the parts after it: the screen, then the LEDs, then the holo. A scene applied starts and ends as one applied any other way: Event carries its scene_started, and its scene_ended with why it ended; Status's scene shows it while it runs to its end.

items.title: Screen
items.text:
r2.holo.Screen.0.1, on screen: what the screen shows, and its backlight, as POST /api/v1/screen/show, DELETE /api/v1/screen and PATCH /api/v1/screen do.

Field Type What it is show uint8 0 leave what shows, 1 a file, 2 a colour, 3 the calibration crosshair, 4 nothing (a clip stops; the panel sleeps with its backlight off) loop bool A file that is a clip or an animation: play it forever. Not with loops loops uint16 A clip or an animation: play it this many times, 1–1000. 0: a clip once, an animated GIF as the file says whole_frame bool A file: decode each frame whole, rather than streamed in blocks colour Colour A colour: which backlight uint8[<=1] Percent, 0–100, until the board next starts. Empty: as it is. With show 0, this is all the request does path uavcan.file.Path.2.0 A file: a QuickTime Motion-JPEG clip (.mov), a PNG, a baseline JPEG or a GIF

The board runs the code POST /api/v1/screen/show runs for a file, a colour or the crosshair, DELETE /api/v1/screen's for nothing, and then, if backlight is given, PATCH /api/v1/screen's. The file is checked before the response, so a refusal means the screen didn't change, and the backlight is set only once what shows has been done. show 0 with no backlight changes nothing, and is answered ok. A path is taken as the HTTP API takes it: from the root of the volume, at most 159 bytes (of the 255 the type has room for), or with the volume's own root in front (/data/clips/intro.mov).

result.code When bad request A path the board refuses ('..' is not allowed in a path: /../a.png, a path may be at most 159 bytes, a path starts with /, …, a control character or a NUL in it), loop with loops (give `loop` (forever) or `loops` (a number of times), not both), loops over 1000, backlight over 100 (`backlight` is 0..100), a show that is none not found No such file (no such file: /clips/a.mov) not playable A file it can't show: the codec, the size, not a clip or an image. The message says which, as the HTTP API's does (/big.png: 400x300 is larger than the 240x240 screen)

items.title: Ring
items.text:
r2.holo.Ring.0.1, on ring: the LED ring, as PATCH /api/v1/leds and the host link's LEDS do. Send only what changes: a new mode starts it from its beginning, a new colour or loop alone restarts the mode running with it, and the brightness applies at once, until the board next starts. A request with nothing in it changes nothing.

Field Type What it is mode uint8[<=1] 0 off, 1 solid, 2 wipe, 3 rainbow, 4 flicker, 5 pulse, 6 blink. Empty: the mode running colour Colour[<=1] For every mode but off and rainbow. Empty: the colour it has (white if it has never had one) loop bool[<=1] Wipe, rainbow: again and again, or once. Empty: once with a new mode; without one, as it is brightness uint8 Percent, 1–100. 0: as it is period_ms uint16 Pulse, blink: 200–60000. 0: pulse 2000, blink 1000

The board runs the code PATCH /api/v1/leds runs, with what the request gives and nothing else, as the host link's LEDS does. brightness is the ring's own brightness (leds bright, GET /api/v1/leds's brightness), the one Light's level is a share of: Ring never sets a level. A new mode starts at level 100, so it undoes a Light's level; a colour, a loop or a period alone keeps the level the ring has, as PATCH /api/v1/leds does. Status's ring shows the product.

result.code When bad request `mode` is off, solid, wipe, rainbow, flicker, pulse or blink (a mode over 6), `brightness` is 1..100, `period_ms` is 200..60000

items.title: ListScenes
items.text:
r2.holo.ListScenes.0.1, on list_scenes: the saved scenes, one a call. Ask for index 0, 1, 2… until the name comes back empty, as uavcan.register.List lists registers. The order is the order they were first saved in (GET /api/v1/scenes).

Field Type What it is index uint8 The request: 0-based count uint8 Scenes saved, 0–16. A save or a delete between calls shifts the list, and this shows it slot uint8 The scene's slot; 0 when it has none name uint8[<=32] Its name; empty once index reaches count

The board counts its saved scenes by their stored lengths alone, in GET /api/v1/scenes' order, and reads and parses only the one asked for, so a call costs about the same whatever its index. result is ok, or busy with the board's queue full, or with the scenes not readable at that moment (busy: the scenes can't be read now); count is then 0. A saved scene that doesn't parse, which only a restored backup could bring (the board checks a scene before saving it), is counted, and answered busy at its index; GET /api/v1/scenes leaves it out instead.

items.title: MediaInfo
items.text:
r2.holo.MediaInfo.0.1, on media_info: a clip's or an image's details from its header, without showing it, as GET /api/v1/media/info gives them. Optional: for a controller that needs more than the names and sizes uavcan.file.List and uavcan.file.GetInfo give.

Field Type What it is path uavcan.file.Path.2.0 The request kind uint8 0 not a clip or an image, 1 clip, 2 image, 3 animation format uint8 0 none, 1 mov, 2 PNG, 3 JPEG, 4 GIF width, height uint16 Pixels frames uint16 A clip or an animation: in one pass; 1 for an image fps float16 A clip or an animation; 0 for an image duration_ms uint32 A clip or an animation: one pass; 0 for an image

result.code is 0 when the board can show it. A file it can't show is not playable, with why in the message, and still described when it is a kind the board knows. (The HTTP API answers that case with 200 and playable: false.) No such file is not found.

The board reads the file's header with the code GET /api/v1/media/info runs, with its checks and words:

result.code When bad request No path (give `path`, from the root of the volume: /clips/intro.mov), or one the board refuses, in the HTTP API's words ('..' is not allowed in a path: /../a.png) not found no such file or directory: /clips/a.mov not playable <path>: <why>, the words of the HTTP API's why (/big400.png: 400x300 is larger than the 240x240 screen), cut to 64 bytes; a file that is no clip or image at all (/notes.txt: not a clip or an image (.mov, .png, .jpg, .gif)), and a directory, with kind 0 and every field 0 busy The second worker already holds two requests

An image is 1 frame, 0 fps and 0 ms, a GIF of one frame among them. Reading a header can take a while (a JPEG is read whole, and a GIF's every frame is looked at), so MediaInfo is carried out with Scene and Screen requests, by the second worker, never holding up the setpoints: on the bench a median of 16 ms over the 45 clips and images in the board's tree, 125 ms for an 837 KB GIF of 30 frames. What a header is read into is PSRAM first, so a MediaInfo takes little of the internal RAM a playing clip needs (4 to 9 KB, where it took up to 29 KB before 2026-11-21: the GIF decoder, the clip's tables, the JPEG's bytes and libpng's state; a JPEG's decoder stays in internal RAM).

items.title: The files
items.text:
uavcan.file.List.0.2 (service 406) and uavcan.file.GetInfo.0.2 (405), the standard services, over the board's storage volume: what fs ls and the HTTP API's /api/v1/media see. Nothing on Cyphal writes, moves or deletes a file: there is no uavcan.file.Read, Write or Modify.

Paths are from the volume's root, /, as in the rest of this interface and in the HTTP API, with its rules (at most 159 bytes, no .., no empty part; the volume's own root in front is taken too). An empty path is the root as well, and a / at the end of a directory's path, as uavcan.file.Path's convention has it, is optional.

List gives a directory's entries one a call: entry_index 0, 1, 2… until entry_base_name comes back empty. They are in byte order of their names, directories among them, each with a / after its name, so a client tells them apart without a GetInfo: the order the storage volume (littlefs) keeps a directory in, and so the order fs ls prints and GET /api/v1/media walks. A directory that doesn't exist, a path that is a file or that the board refuses, and an index past the last all give the empty name: the type has no other answer. A call reads the directory's names up to its index, about 0.1 ms an entry on the board: on the bench, the root's 44 entries (43 files and a directory) took 3.8 ms a call at index 0 and 8.4 ms at index 43, from a computer, against 3.5 ms for a uavcan.node.GetInfo. An entry added or removed between two calls shifts the ones after it, as the type warns.

GetInfo gives an entry's details:

Field On this board error OK; NOT_FOUND (2) for no such file or directory; INVALID_VALUE (22) for a path the board refuses; IO_ERROR (5) for anything else, and when the board's queue of requests is full (try again) size Bytes; 0 for a directory unix_timestamp_of_last_modification When the file was last written, if the board's clock had been set by then (from the network); 0 otherwise is_file_not_directory As it says is_link Always false is_readable True is_writeable False: nothing on Cyphal writes a file

Both are carried out by the second worker, with Scene, Screen and MediaInfo requests, since either waits for the storage volume, which an upload over Wi-Fi holds through each write (on the bench, during a 1 MB upload, a List of the root's last entry took 82 ms in the median and up to half a second); so one may wait behind a MediaInfo or a still being shown. A GetInfo takes about 1.5 ms on the board at rest. With the board's queue full, GetInfo answers IO_ERROR, and List isn't answered at all: its empty name would read as the end of the list, and it carries no count, so the client times out and asks again.

items.title: Error
items.text:
r2.holo.Error.0.1, the result of every service. code is the host link's status, with the same numbers. A busy answer's message is busy: the board is still working through earlier requests (four of them, or for Scene, Screen and MediaInfo, two of those):

code Name The JSON errors it covers 0 ok — 1 bad request bad_request, bad_path 2 not found not_found, unknown_scene, not_running 3 not playable not_playable 4 not ready not_ready: the holo can't move 5 busy busy, and the board's queue of Cyphal requests full: try again 6 failed Anything else Field Type What it is code uint8 Above reason Reason With not ready: why, and the axis. With ok: only for a leia whose centre was refused. NONE otherwise message uint8[<=64] The JSON error's message, word for word, cut to 64 bytes. Empty with ok, except as reason says

A response that is ok is 3 bytes, one frame (4 for Light).

items.title: Reason
items.text:
r2.holo.Reason.0.1, one byte: the holo engine's reasons, with the words the console and the JSON API use.

why Means 0 None 1 not fitted: the axis's servo isn't there 2 not armed (no arm switch on this board) 3 uncalibrated: the axis has no saved endpoints and the holo needs them 4 unknown axis 5 no light (never on this board, whose ring is its light) 15 Another reason: the message says

axis: 0 none in particular, 1 horizontal (pan), 2 vertical (tilt), 3 the light's channel (a panel's holo only).

items.title: Registers
items.text:
Read and written with uavcan.register.Access and listed with uavcan.register.List, by any Cyphal tool. The console's cyphal register reads and writes the same table, with the same checks. Every mutable register is saved on the board, in NVS, as soon as it is written, and is part of a backup; none holds a credential. List gives them in the order of the tables below: the node's three, then each port's .id and .type, then the holo's seven.

A write the board can't take leaves the register as it was, and the response, which always carries the register's value after the write, shows it: a value out of range or not a name, one of another type, a port number another port has (below), or a .type register. A number of another type is taken when it converts exactly (a natural8, an integer64 or a real32 52 all write 52 to uavcan.node.id), and the name takes unstructured bytes as well as a string. A register that doesn't exist reads empty, and a write to one does nothing. The board's log says what was written and by which node, or why it wasn't. While the board is still writing earlier requests (four at once), another write is answered with the register as it is, unwritten: send it again.

The node:

Register Type Values Default Flags Takes effect uavcan.node.id natural16[1] 0–127, or 65535 for plug-and-play. Anything else is refused 65535 mutable, persistent When the node next starts r2.node.name string The name GetInfo reports: 1–50 characters, as cyphal name takes it r2.dome.holo.front mutable, persistent When the node next starts uavcan.can.bitrate natural32[2] The first value is the bitrate: 125000, 250000, 500000 or 1000000. The second (CAN FD's data phase) is ignored, and reads back as the first [1000000, 1000000] mutable, persistent When the node next starts

These are the settings cyphal id, cyphal name and cyphal bitrate change: either way changes both. The name isn't uavcan.node.description: that standard register is a free-text note that doesn't change what GetInfo reports, and this one does.

The ports, one pair a port name (status, event, axes, setpoint, motion, light, scene, screen, ring, list_scenes, media_info):

Register Type Values Default Flags Takes effect uavcan.pub.<name>.id, uavcan.sub.<name>.id, uavcan.srv.<name>.id natural16[1] A subject-ID 0–8191 or a service-ID 0–511; 65535 turns the port off The default mutable, persistent When the node next starts uavcan.pub.<name>.type, and so on string The type, r2.holo.Status.0.1 — immutable, persistent —

So uavcan.pub.status.id is 2300 until written, and uavcan.srv.motion.type reads r2.holo.Motion.0.1. The .type registers let a tool such as Yakut call a service by its port name. The standard suggests 65535 as every port's default; the board starts with working defaults instead, so it can be used without configuring anything. The special registers for a register's minimum, maximum and default (<name><, <name>>, <name>=) aren't provided.

A number belongs to one port. Subject-IDs are one set, published and subscribed alike (a subscription on a subject the board publishes would take other nodes' messages of that type for its own), and service-IDs another. Within each, a number is one of the node's own fixed ports' (subjects 7509, 7510 and 8166, services 384, 385, 405, 406, 430 and 435) or one r2.holo port's, never two: a write of a number another port has is refused with the port that has it ("subject 2301 is uavcan.pub.event.id's"), and the register keeps its value. A subject and a service may share a number, and any number of ports may be off (65535). So two ports swap through a free number, or through off. A saved number that breaks the rule anyway, which only a configuration from elsewhere can bring (a backup from another firmware), turns the later port in the table off as the board starts, with a warning in its log; its register then reads 65535.

The holo:

Register Type Values Default Flags Takes effect r2.holo.horizontal.endpoints_us, r2.holo.vertical.endpoints_us natural16[2] Closed, then open, in µs, each within the servo's absolute range (1000–2000 on this board) and not equal; closed above open turns the axis round. [0, 0] goes back to the firmware's default range, and clears the drive policy with it [1150, 1900], [1300, 1950]: the default range, not saved mutable, persistent At once: the next motion uses them r2.holo.horizontal.release, r2.holo.vertical.release bit[3] The drive policy, for the closed end, the open end and between (the ends are 2 % of the travel wide): true lets the servo go once it has settled, false keeps driving it [false, false, false] mutable, persistent At the servo's next frame r2.holo.horizontal.settle_ms, r2.holo.vertical.settle_ms natural16[1] How long a command is driven before a release takes effect: 0–65535, under 100 raised to 100 100 mutable, persistent At once r2.touch.reporting bit[1] Touch events on or off false (true in a build with BOARD_TOUCH_AUTOSTART) mutable, persistent At once, and at every start

The endpoints are the ones holo endpoints sets, and the drive policy the one the web app and PUT /api/v1/servos/policy set: the same saved values, the servos' own, so a change either way shows the other way. Two rules come with them from the servos: clearing the endpoints ([0, 0], as holo endpoints <axis> clear and DELETE /api/v1/servos/calibration do) clears the drive policy too, back to holding everywhere and 100 ms; and a drive policy once saved has a settle time of 100 ms at least, so a release written over a policy never saved also saves 100 ms. Status's horizontal and vertical say whether each axis is calibrated and turned round. An axis whose servo isn't fitted reads [0, 0], [false, false, false] and 0, and refuses a write (the axis has no servo (not fitted)). A refused write keeps the register as it was, with the reason on the console (closed and open are each 1000 to 2000 us, and not the same; [0, 0] goes back to the default range, a settle time is 0 to 65535 ms).

A read of these six over Cyphal is carried out by the node's worker, as a write is, from the servos themselves (reading them can wait on a save in progress, which the node's own task mustn't): a change made on the console or over HTTP reads over Cyphal at once. With the board's queue of requests full, such a read isn't answered (uavcan.register.Access has no way to say busy), and the client asks again.

r2.touch.reporting is one of the board's settings: the same one as touch.reporting in /api/v1/settings and the console's settings touch. A write turns touch reporting on or off at once and saves it, so that a controller sets it once, and the board starts with touch reporting on or off as it says; DELETE /api/v1/settings and a factory reset put it back to its default. touch on and touch off on the console change it for the moment without saving; the register reads what is in effect, so after a touch off it reads false until it is written or the board restarts. It isn't a credential or an identity, so it is in a backup (NVS holo_cfg, touch, with the board's other settings).

items.title: Commands
items.text:
uavcan.node.ExecuteCommand.1.3, on service 435:

Command Number Does Restart 65535 Restarts the board a second after the response (by when it has gone). The node comes back with the registers as they now are Factory reset 65532 The node's registers back to their defaults (the node-ID, name and bitrate, every port), as cyphal reset does, and the board's settings to theirs (the boot scene, the backlight, the LEDs' brightness and count, touch reporting, which is the register r2.touch.reporting), as DELETE /api/v1/settings does; then a restart, a second after the response. Kept: the scenes, the files, the servos' calibration and drive policy (their registers keep their values), the network and the web app's settings, and the host link's mode and pins, so the node is still on the bus afterwards, asking for a node-ID by plug-and-play Identify 65529 The ring blinks white, once a second, and the screen shows the crosshair for 5 seconds, then both go back to what they were doing Store persistent states 65530 Nothing to do: every register is saved when it is written. Answers success Anything else Refused: bad command. Power off, begin software update and emergency stop included

A response's status is success when the command was taken, before a restart; failure when the board is still working through four earlier requests, or for identify, which is carried out with the Scene and Screen requests, two of those (send it again); internal error if a factory reset couldn't save, in which case nothing is reset (what was saved before is put back) and the board doesn't restart. output is always empty.

Identify is a five-second scene, identify, applied as a scene of the board's own would be: the web app, the HTTP API's GET /api/v1/scenes and the events show it running, and it ends a scene that is running to its end. At its end the screen, the ring and the holo go back to what they were doing before it, as with any scene whose then is restore (a twitch or a scan starts again; a clip on its way to its end doesn't), or, if it ended a scene that restores, to what that scene would have restored.

items.title: Sizes and bus load
items.text:
Each type's size, from its definition ("least" with every variable-length field empty). A frame is about 130 bits on the wire, so 130 µs at 1 Mbit/s.

Type Least: bytes, frames Worst case: bytes, frames Status 86, 13 375, 54 Event 5, 1 265, 39 Axes 4, 1 4, 1 Motion request 17, 3 19, 3 Light request 8, 2 12, 2 Scene request 3, 1 35, 6 Screen request 9, 2 265, 39 Ring request 6, 1 11, 2 ListScenes request, response 1, 1; 6, 1 1, 1; 102, 15 MediaInfo request, response 1, 1; 17, 3 256, 37; 81, 12 uavcan.file.List request, response 9, 2; 5, 1 264, 38; 260, 38 uavcan.file.GetInfo request, response 1, 1; 13, 3 256, 37; 13, 3 Any other response 3, 1 67, 10 (a refusal with a 64-byte message)

The worst cases with a path count 255 bytes; this board's paths are at most 159. In practice a Status with a 20-byte path and a 10-byte scene name is 116 bytes, 17 frames; an event with a 20-byte path, 4 or 5.

What the board sends, at 1 Mbit/s:

Traffic Frames a second Share of the bus Heartbeat, once a second 1 0.013 % Port list, 24 frames every 10 s 2.4 0.03 % Status once a second, 17 frames (13 with nothing showing and no scene) 17 0.22 % Status four times a second (while things change) 68 0.88 % Axes while moving, ten a second 10 0.13 % Axes at rest 1 0.013 % All of it, while moving and changing about 81 about 1.1 %

A controller streaming setpoints at 50 a second adds 50 frames, 0.65 %. The board hands its frames to the CAN controller one at a time, highest priority first, so a setpoint's echo in axes or a service's response waits behind at most one frame of a long Status, not the whole of it.

items.title: Not on Cyphal
items.text:
These stay on Wi-Fi, the USB console, or the host link:

  • Uploading clips and images, and deleting or moving files.
  • The network, the web app's settings, and any password or token.
  • The configuration backup (nvs_export, nvs_import).
  • Firmware updates: over Wi-Fi, as now.
  • Saving, changing and deleting scenes, and applying a scene given whole: the web app and the HTTP API do those. Cyphal applies a saved one.
  • The board's settings (the boot scene and the levels it starts with) other than by a factory reset, and the host link's own settings.
  • Raw servo moves, for finding endpoints: the web app's calibration, servo_move and holo endpoints do that. The endpoints themselves are registers.
  • Catching up on missed events: the HTTP API's and the host link's "events after N" has no Cyphal counterpart; Status is the catch-up.
  • Diagnostics on the bus (uavcan.diagnostic.Record), time synchronisation, the IMU and the battery.
  • The console's holo led and holo leia, which still do nothing on this board: the Light service is what drives the ring as the holo's light.

items.title: Host link protocol
items.text:
What's in the firmware so far

JSON lines, native frames and events, on UART and RS485. The I2C register map is described ahead of the firmware.

This is the specification of what goes over the host link: the wire between the board and a controller (another microcontroller, an ESP32, a Raspberry Pi, a dome controller). The wiring for each transport is on its own page: UART, RS485 and I2C.

There are two protocols, and the board can accept both on the same port:

Protocol Looks like For Transports JSON lines POST /scenes/apply {"name":"cantina"} Hosts that can build and read JSON: a Pi, an ESP32, a person at a terminal UART, RS485 Native frames Small binary messages with a CRC Hosts with little memory, and I2C UART, RS485, I2C

JSON lines are the board's HTTP API, one request a line. The requests, replies and errors are the ones that page and its OpenAPI description document. Native frames are a small fixed subset of the same things: scenes, the screen, the LEDs, the holo, and status.

This is protocol version 1. GET /link reports it, as does the native PING.

items.title: A request
items.text:
One line, ending with a line feed (\n, 0x0A). A carriage return before it is ignored, so a terminal's \r\n works.

[@<address> ][#<tag> ]<METHOD> <path>[ <JSON>]
Part What it is @<address> Which board: @12 for address 12, @g3 for group 3, @* for every board. Needed on RS485. Optional on UART, where there is only one board #<tag> Optional. 1–16 of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -. The reply carries it back, so a host can match a reply to its request <METHOD> GET, PUT, POST, PATCH or DELETE, in capitals <path> A path of the HTTP API, without /api/v1: /scenes/apply, /scenes/scene?name=cantina. A path with /api/v1 in front is accepted too <JSON> The request body, on the same line: a JSON object, as the HTTP API takes it. Left out when the request has none

A line is at most 1024 bytes, including the line feed, and is UTF-8. An empty line is ignored.

GET /screen
PATCH /leds {"mode":"solid","colour":"orange","brightness":30}
POST /scenes/apply {"name":"cantina"}
#a7 POST /holo/motion {"motion":"nod","count":2}
@3 POST /scenes/end

items.title: The reply
items.text:
[@<address> ][#<tag> ]<status>[ +<pending>][ <JSON>]
Part What it is @<address> The board's own address, when the request had one #<tag> The request's tag, when it had one <status> The HTTP status, three digits: 200, 202, 204, 400, 404, 409, 422, … +<pending> How many events are waiting for the host (see Events). Only there when it isn't 0 <JSON> The reply body, as the HTTP API sends it. There is none with 204

An error is the status with the API's error object:

> POST /screen/show {"path":"/clips/nope.mov"}
< 404 {"error":"not_found","message":"no /clips/nope.mov"}
> #a8 POST /holo/motion {"motion":"wag"}
< #a8 409 +1 {"error":"not_ready","message":"the holo is not armed"}

(> is what the host sends, and < what the board sends back. Neither is sent.)

On top of the HTTP API's errors, a line can get:
